description:
Attorney General Todd Blanche told CNN’s “State of the Union” today that members of the House Oversight Committee should be “very worried,” after President Donald Trump tasked the Department of Justice with investigating Democrats. 

It comes after Trump said Saturday he would have the DOJ look into threats of “Impeachment and many other forms of punishment” by Democrats against certain members of his administration, companies and donors to his ballroom project. 

Incoming House Oversight Committee Chair Rep. Robert Garcia (D-CA) and senior Oversight Committee member Rep. Stephen Lynch (D-MA) respond to Blanche's threat.

author: CNN
description:
In a setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his main rival will be tasked with forming the next Israeli government, placing him one step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving leader, even as the path remains complicated. 

Gadi Eisenkot, a retired military chief who led the centrist Yashar party in the October 27 election, will have up to six weeks to try and assemble a coalition to replace Netanyahu. But his path to power is fraught with political obstacles and divisions within the opposition itself.  

CNN's Oren Liebermann reports from Jerusalem and CNN's Salma Abdelaziz gets analysis from International Crisis Group's Mairav Zonszein. Also, CNN's Brian Abel speaks with Haaretz reporter Joshua Leifer about what's next for Benjamin Netanyahu. 

0:00 Gadi Eisenkot tapped by Israeli president to form the country's next government 
1:40 CNN's Oren Liebermann on Eisenkot's path to forming a coalition government 
4:35 Will Arab parties play a role in Eisenkot's coalition? 
9:2
title: Eisenkot one step closer to ousting Netanyahu

author: CNN
description:
Some content in this episode may be distressing to some viewers.

W. Kamau Bell heads down south to meet with members of the Ku Klux Klan looking to rebrand their message.

In his own words: “I’m getting email from the Ku Klux Klan. It’s OK though. It’s totally my fault, because I’m the one who went and paid them a visit. I even went to a cross lighting. (They don’t call it a cross burning, like the rest of us.) And it all happened in the first episode of my CNN show “United Shades of America”. The idea behind the series is to send an African-American comedian to places that you wouldn’t expect him to go or to places where he absolutely shouldn’t go.”

Follow comedian and political gadfly W. Kamau Bell as he explores the far corners of our country and its various groups and subcultures.
